source_caveats.finding: The title page identifies the thirteenth edition. Copyright says2023; EPUB dc:date says2022-07-06. These are different metadata facts, not interchangeable publication dates. OPF identifier7130806 is retained as opaque despite its identifier-type metadata.
source_caveats.treatment: Canonical authors and printed ISBN come from title/copyright pages. Exact commercial release date is not independently established.

source_caveats.finding: Brief contents calls chapter1 The Changing Role..., while the body and detailed contents use The Crucial Role.... Chapter11 body uses Flexible Budgeting and Analysis of Overhead Costs; contents variants use Flexible Budgeting and the Management of Overhead and Support Activity Costs.
source_caveats.treatment: Retain actual body titles and the complete short contents-label inventory; do not silently standardize source titles.

source_caveats.finding: Weighted-average method is substantively taught. FIFO is mentioned but detailed FIFO procedures are not developed in the inspected treatment. Subsequent production departments are also deferred rather than developed here.
source_caveats.treatment: Provide a weighted-average first-department model only; do not invent a source-supported FIFO or transferred-in-cost implementation.

source_caveats.finding: Purchase-price variances and usage-basis price variances have different quantity bases. Fixed-overhead volume is an allocation difference, and the authors use positive/negative terminology rather than treating its sign as an automatic performance verdict.
source_caveats.treatment: Keep separate executable models; require compatible basis for totals. Full material mix/yield variance decompositions are not developed by this library from the selected source treatment.

source_caveats.finding: The image ufig15-10.png beneath the General Formula discussion appears to repeat a total-variable-cost markup formula.
source_caveats.treatment: Preserve this source-formatting question. The general excluded-cost markup equation in the library is explicitly an analytical generalization, not a literal transcription or silent correction.

source_caveats.topic: Full allocated fixed cost as an opportunity-cost proxy
source_caveats.finding: The chapter15 competitive-bidding discussion uses allocated capacity-producing fixed cost as a proxy in its capacity context; chapter14 relevant-cost reasoning identifies the actual benefit forgone.
source_caveats.treatment: Retain the source distinction and qualify the proxy. Require project evidence of alternative use; do not replace actual opportunity cost with an allocation by default.

source_caveats.finding: The edition discusses reinvestment assumptions, perfect capital markets and limits on ranking independent projects. These are retained as author framing under its assumptions.
source_caveats.treatment: The NPV function simply discounts supplied dated cash flows and does not fabricate reinvestment proceeds. Broad ranking language is not elevated to a universal impossibility theorem; external adjudication was not performed.

source_caveats.topic: Tax, accounting policy, law, software and historical examples
source_caveats.finding: Source-era internal-control rules, tax examples and company illustrations are historical exposition, not current verified requirements. Cited studies were not independently read.
source_caveats.treatment: No current external verification is claimed. Operational policy, tax rates, depreciation, financing and software behavior require supplied authority or separate current verification.

coverage_gaps: Selected passages across all chapters are represented, not every section or supporting numerical exhibit.
Most case narratives, exercises, problems, worked solutions and cited primary studies were not read substantively; presence is inventoried only.
FIFO, advanced transferred-in process-cost calculations and detailed material mix/yield decompositions are not supplied as if taught here.
Linear programming and theory of constraints are explained conceptually; no general LP solver is implemented. Multiple regression, learning curves and real options are not implemented.
No full company-specific master budget, multivariate forecast or tax engine is supplied; component models require definitions, timing and opening balances.
No operational project evidence, company accounting policy or external-library IDs have been invented.
Current legal, tax, accounting-standard, software, market and company facts were not independently verified.

No assertion that automated text similarity establishes semantic quality.
editorial_review.confidence_policy: Source confidence reflects selected passage fidelity; there is no imposed confidence distribution. Confidence does not imply numerical testing or project suitability.
